About the Position

Forestry graduate students learn from a dynamic and diverse group of researchers who educate and communicate how forests and the products that are created from them contribute to the well-being of all living things. The health and sustainability of forests and the people who depend on them underlies everything we do. UBC is among the best institutions globally in forest-related education and research and is also unique in the breadth of expertise, which allows integration of new knowledge across many disciplines.

PhD in Forestry students can be found all over the world; they are important ambassadors for UBC Forestry and demonstrate just how diverse and international in scope the research is that is undertaken in the Faculty. There are approximately 130 doctoral students in any given year, which is about 40% of the total Forestry graduate student population. In addition to being part of the Faculty of Forestry, PhD students are also considered members of one of the three Faculty departments, based on their supervisor's affiliation.

Program Structure

The major requirement for the PhD in Forestry is completion of a research dissertation which meets the requirements of the Faculty of Graduate & Post-doctoral Studies. Advancement to Candidacy must be achieved within 24 months of the start of studies, the requirements of which include a comprehensive examination. Course work is not required for the Forestry PhD, although many doctoral students do complete courses (either for credit or audit) as recommended by their supervisory committee.

Financial Support

All full-time students in UBC-Vancouver PhD programs will be provided with a funding package of at least $40,000 for each of the first four years of their PhD from September 2026. The funding package may consist of any combination of internal or external awards, teaching-related work, research assistantships, and graduate academic assistantships.

Based on funding statistics, 111 students within this program were included in a study because they received funding through UBC in the form of teaching, research, academic assistantships or internal or external awards with a mean of $43,193 and a median of $44,166. This results in a net balance (any funding provided to the student minus tuition and fees) mean of $34,192 and median of $34,113.

Important Notes

  • All full-time UBC PhD students receive a minimum of $40,000 per year in funding for the first four years (from September 2026).
  • International students enrolled as full-time students with a valid study permit can work on campus for unlimited hours and work off-campus for no more than 24 hours a week during academic sessions.
  • Application deadlines for May 2027 intake: 1 October 2026 for both Canadian and International applicants.

How to Apply

Submit your application through the official portal before the deadline: 1 October 2026. Read the eligibility requirements carefully and prepare all requested documents — early applications are strongly recommended for competitive awards.
